title: Inside a Four-Stroke Engine
objective: Connect piston movement and valve timing to a complete two-revolution cycle.

stages.title: Whole engine
stages.text: A piston connects through a rod to a rotating crankshaft. The camshaft times the valves.

stages.title: Intake
stages.text: The intake valve opens as the piston descends, drawing in a fresh charge.

stages.title: Compression
stages.text: Both valves close as the piston rises. The trapped charge is compressed.

stages.title: Power
stages.text: Ignition near the top starts combustion. Expanding gas pushes the piston down and turns the crank.

stages.title: Exhaust
stages.text: The exhaust valve opens as the piston rises, pushing spent gas out.

limits: Ideal spark-ignition cylinder; valve overlap and advance omitted. Positions are schematic, not a pressure prediction.
misconception: The spark does not push the piston mechanically; expanding hot gas does.

terms.Charge: The fresh air and fuel mixture in this example.

title: How Bicycle Gears Work
objective: Relate sprocket tooth counts to wheel turns and required pedal torque.

stages.title: Drivetrain
stages.text: A chain connects a front chainring to a rear sprocket.

stages.title: Pedal input
stages.text: One crank turn moves one chainring circumference of chain.

stages.title: Wheel output
stages.text: A smaller rear sprocket turns more times for the same chain travel.

stages.title: Trade-off
stages.text: Higher gearing travels farther per pedal turn but requires more input torque for the same wheel torque.

limits: Ideal chain drive, 2.1 m wheel circumference and 60 rpm cadence; no friction, slopes or tire slip.
misconception: Gears trade force for distance; they do not create energy.

terms.Gear ratio: Front teeth divided by rear teeth.

title: How Hydraulic Brakes Work
objective: Trace pressure transmission and distinguish pressure from force.

stages.title: Brake system
stages.text: Pedal, master piston, fluid line and caliper connect the driver to a disc.

stages.title: Master cylinder
stages.text: An input force pressurizes the nearly incompressible fluid.

stages.title: Caliper
stages.text: The pressure acts over a larger piston area, producing greater force and less travel.

stages.title: Disc
stages.text: Pads press the disc. Friction converts motion energy into heat.

limits: 100 N master-piston force over 1 cm²; ideal sealed system. Pedal leverage, compliance and pad friction omitted.
misconception: Hydraulics multiply force, not work; the output piston moves less.

terms.Caliper: Holds pistons and pads around the brake disc.

title: How a Refrigerator Moves Heat
objective: Trace the refrigerant loop and account for heat discharged into the room.

stages.title: Closed loop
stages.text: Refrigerant carries energy through four components; it is not used up.

stages.title: Evaporator
stages.text: Low-pressure refrigerant absorbs heat from the cabinet and evaporates.

stages.title: Compressor
stages.text: Electrical work raises vapor pressure and temperature.

stages.title: Condenser
stages.text: Hot refrigerant releases heat into the room and condenses.

stages.title: Expansion
stages.text: A restriction drops pressure before refrigerant returns to the evaporator.

limits: Conceptual vapor-compression cycle. No refrigerant-specific temperatures or efficiency predictions.
misconception: A refrigerator moves heat; it does not manufacture cold.

title: How an Air Conditioner Works
objective: Connect thermostat demand, airflow and the refrigeration loop.

stages.title: Two spaces
stages.text: Indoor and outdoor coils exchange heat through a closed refrigerant loop.

stages.title: Demand
stages.text: When indoor temperature exceeds the setting, the controller calls for cooling.

stages.title: Indoor coil
stages.text: Air passes the cold evaporator; heat enters the refrigerant.

stages.title: Outdoor coil
stages.text: Compressor and condenser release the indoor heat plus electrical work outdoors.

stages.title: Satisfied
stages.text: Cooling stops when the thermostat is satisfied in this simple controller.

limits: Indoor air fixed at 26 °C for comparison. On/off control; humidity, hysteresis and inverter modulation omitted.
misconception: The outdoor unit rejects heat; it does not simply blow indoor air outside.

terms.Thermostat: Controller comparing temperature to a setting.

title: How a Washing Machine Works
objective: Distinguish cleaning, pumping and spin extraction.

stages.title: Machine
stages.text: A perforated drum sits inside a water-holding tub.

stages.title: Fill
stages.text: The inlet admits water; detergent helps suspend soil.

stages.title: Wash
stages.text: Drum movement repeatedly moves fabric through wash water.

stages.title: Drain
stages.text: A pump removes used water from the tub.

stages.title: Spin
stages.text: Fast rotation presses fabric outward; water passes through drum holes into the tub and is pumped away.

limits: Representative front-loading machine. No exact timings, balance sensing or real control logic.
misconception: Spinning does not dry by heating; it extracts much of the liquid water.

title: How an Elevator Works
objective: Explain how a counterweight reduces the motor’s load.

stages.title: Traction system
stages.text: Ropes pass over a driven sheave between car and counterweight.

stages.title: Request
stages.text: Controls select a destination and keep doors interlocked.

stages.title: Motion
stages.text: The motor turns the sheave. Car and counterweight move in opposite directions.

stages.title: Arrival
stages.text: Controls slow the car, stop at a landing and permit doors to open.

stages.title: Protection
stages.text: Brakes, overspeed protection and buffers are separate layers; this diagram does not simulate them.

limits: Ideal 1:1 traction arrangement, not construction or maintenance guidance. Safety systems shown conceptually.
misconception: The motor does not lift the entire car weight unopposed; a counterweight balances part of it.

terms.Interlock: Prevents unsafe door and car operation.

title: How a Lock and Key Work
objective: Explain the shear line in normal pin-tumbler operation.

stages.title: Lock
stages.text: A plug rotates inside a fixed shell. Pin stacks cross the boundary.

stages.title: Key enters
stages.text: The normal matching key raises each stack by its designed amount.

stages.title: Alignment
stages.text: Boundaries between key pins and driver pins align at the shear line.

stages.title: Turn
stages.text: With the line clear, the plug can rotate and operate the latch.

limits: Conceptual cutaway for ordinary operation only. No picking, bypass, dimensions or security rating.
misconception: A key does not merely fill the slot; its profile must align the pin boundaries.

terms.Shear line: Boundary between rotating plug and fixed shell.

title: How Levers and Pulleys Help Us Lift
objective: Compare ideal input force, travel and mechanical work.

stages.title: Simple machines
stages.text: A lever pivots about a fulcrum; pulleys redirect rope tension.

stages.title: Lever
stages.text: A longer effort arm reduces the force needed for the same load torque.

stages.title: Pulley
stages.text: Several supporting rope segments share the load.

stages.title: Conservation
stages.text: Less force requires more input distance. Ideal input and output work match.

limits: 100 N load lifted 0.2 m, ideal massless ropes and frictionless pivots.
misconception: Mechanical advantage does not provide free energy.

terms.Work: Force times distance along the force direction.

title: How a Jet Engine Produces Thrust
objective: Connect rearward momentum flow to forward thrust.

stages.title: Turbojet
stages.text: Air passes through a compressor, combustor, turbine and nozzle.

stages.title: Compress
stages.text: Rotating blades raise air pressure; they need shaft power.

stages.title: Burn
stages.text: Fuel burns in the compressed flow, adding energy.

stages.title: Turbine
stages.text: Hot gas turns a turbine linked by shaft to the compressor.

stages.title: Exhaust
stages.text: The nozzle accelerates gas rearward; the engine experiences forward thrust.

limits: Simplified turbojet, not a turbofan. No calculated thrust or real operating limits.
misconception: The turbine extracts power for the compressor; the exhaust momentum change produces thrust.

terms.Thrust: Force associated with changing flow momentum.
terms.Turbine: Blades extracting energy from hot flowing gas.

title: How Electricity Reaches Your Home
objective: Trace the grid and explain why transmission uses high voltage.

stages.title: Grid
stages.text: Generators, lines, substations and local circuits form a connected system.

stages.title: Step up
stages.text: A transformer raises AC voltage for transmission.

stages.title: Transmit
stages.text: For the same power, higher voltage means lower current and lower resistive loss.

stages.title: Step down
stages.text: Substations and distribution transformers lower voltage for local use.

stages.title: Home
stages.text: A meter records energy; a panel distributes power to protected branch circuits.

limits: Single-path illustration, 1 Ω line and P = VI with unity power factor. Real grids have AC impedance and many paths.
misconception: Electricity is not stored in transmission wires like water in a tank.

terms.Transformer: Changes AC voltage using magnetic induction.
terms.kWh: A unit of energy, not power.

title: How a Battery Stores and Supplies Energy
objective: Distinguish external electron flow from internal ion movement.

stages.title: Cell
stages.text: Two electrodes and an electrolyte enable a chemical energy conversion.

stages.title: Discharge
stages.text: Chemical reactions drive electrons through the external load.

stages.title: Inside
stages.text: Ions move in the electrolyte to balance charge; a separator prevents direct contact.

stages.title: Charge
stages.text: An external charger drives the rechargeable reactions in the opposite direction.

limits: Generic rechargeable-cell schematic. Electrode chemistry and quantitative charge rates omitted.
misconception: Electrons travel through the external circuit; ions carry charge through the electrolyte.

title: How Solar Panels Generate Electricity
objective: Connect light absorption, direct current and AC conversion.

stages.title: System
stages.text: PV modules connect to power electronics and loads.

stages.title: Cell
stages.text: Absorbed light can free charge carriers in a semiconductor.

stages.title: DC
stages.text: The cell structure separates charges; an external circuit carries direct current.

stages.title: Inverter
stages.text: Power electronics convert DC to AC for compatible household use.

stages.title: Storage
stages.text: An optional battery stores energy through its own controlled charging path.

limits: Illustrative 1 kW array under reference full light; linear light scaling, no temperature, shading or conversion losses.
misconception: Solar PV uses light, not heat; a battery is optional.

title: How a Wind Turbine Generates Electricity
objective: Follow energy from moving air to generator output.

stages.title: Wind system
stages.text: Airflow, rotor, shaft and generator form an energy-conversion chain.

stages.title: Lift
stages.text: Air flowing around shaped blades creates forces that turn the rotor.

stages.title: Generator
stages.text: Shaft rotation produces electrical output through electromagnetic induction.

stages.title: Control
stages.text: Pitch and other controls limit loads; turbines stop outside safe operating conditions.

limits: Invented normalized teaching curve: cut-in 3 m/s, rated 12 m/s, cut-out 25 m/s. Not specifications for any turbine.
misconception: More wind does not mean unlimited output; controls cap power and can stop operation.

terms.Lift: Aerodynamic force perpendicular to relative airflow.
terms.Cut-out: Wind speed at which a turbine shuts down for protection.

title: How an Electric Motor Turns
objective: Relate changing coil current to a continuing turning effect.

stages.title: DC motor
stages.text: A coil sits between magnetic poles and connects through brushes and a split-ring commutator.

stages.title: Force
stages.text: Current-carrying coil sides experience opposite magnetic forces.

stages.title: Torque
stages.text: The pair of forces turns the coil around its shaft.

stages.title: Commutation
stages.text: The split ring reverses coil current each half-turn so torque keeps its turning sense.

limits: Simplified brushed DC motor, schematic current timing; no inertia, friction or speed prediction.
misconception: A motor needs energy input; magnets alone do not supply continuous work.

title: How a Generator Makes Electricity
objective: Connect changing magnetic flux to induced voltage.

stages.title: Generator
stages.text: Mechanical input rotates a coil in a magnetic field.

stages.title: Flux
stages.text: As the coil turns, the magnetic flux through it changes.

stages.title: Induction
stages.text: A changing flux induces voltage across the coil.

stages.title: Output
stages.text: Reversing rotation reverses the instantaneous voltage; faster rotation raises its amplitude in this model.

limits: Single ideal coil with normalized voltage. E = −N dΦ/dt; no load torque or real volts.
misconception: A stationary coil in an unchanging field has no sustained induced voltage.

terms.Flux: Magnetic field passing through an area.
terms.Induction: Voltage caused by changing magnetic flux.

title: How a Household Circuit Works
objective: Compare series and parallel current paths in a safe virtual model.

stages.title: Circuit
stages.text: A source, conducting paths, switch and loads form a complete loop.

stages.title: Switch
stages.text: An open switch interrupts its current path.

stages.title: Series
stages.text: Two equal loads in series share source voltage.

stages.title: Parallel
stages.text: Equal parallel loads each receive the full source voltage; their branch currents add.

limits: 12 V virtual DC source and 12 Ω resistors. Household mains use AC; this is not wiring instruction.
misconception: Current is not used up by a load; energy is transferred.

sources.title: OpenStax: resistors in series and parallel

title: How Circuit Breakers and GFCIs Protect People
objective: Distinguish excess current from unequal outgoing and returning current.

stages.title: Protection
stages.text: Different devices detect different conditions.

stages.title: Breaker
stages.text: Overcurrent protection responds to excessive current, with timing depending on device and fault.

stages.title: GFCI
stages.text: A sensor compares current going out and returning.

stages.title: Trip
stages.text: A sufficient imbalance causes a GFCI to disconnect; normal load current alone need not be excessive.

limits: Conceptual outcomes only; no trip time or calibrated threshold. Virtual activity, not an installation or protection test.
misconception: A standard breaker and a GFCI do not detect the same thing.

terms.Overcurrent: Current exceeding a circuit’s permitted conditions.
terms.Imbalance: Difference between outgoing and returning current.

title: How LEDs Produce Light
objective: Connect forward current and charge recombination to light.

stages.title: LED circuit
stages.text: A source, current limiter and LED form a controlled current path.

stages.title: Junction
stages.text: Forward bias allows charge carriers to cross a semiconductor junction.

stages.title: Light
stages.text: Electron-hole recombination can release energy as photons.

stages.title: Limit
stages.text: A resistor or driver keeps current within a suitable range.

limits: Qualitative LED, no real component ratings. Reverse voltage can damage real LEDs; all trials are virtual.
misconception: An LED is not a tiny heated filament; semiconductor transitions produce its light.

title: How an EV Charges
objective: Identify where AC becomes DC and why charging power changes.

stages.title: Charging path
stages.text: Supply, charging equipment, vehicle electronics and battery management cooperate.

stages.title: AC charging
stages.text: An onboard charger converts AC into controlled DC.

stages.title: DC charging
stages.text: External equipment supplies controlled DC, bypassing the onboard AC converter.

stages.title: Battery management
stages.text: The vehicle limits charging to protect cell conditions; power often tapers as the battery fills.

limits: Illustrative paths only. No actual charge time, connector compatibility or power prediction.
misconception: Charging equipment and the car negotiate limits; a high charger rating does not guarantee that power.

title: What Happens When You Open an App
objective: Follow the relationship between storage, memory, CPU and operating system.

stages.title: Computer
stages.text: Storage holds persistent files; memory holds active working data.

stages.title: Load
stages.text: The operating system maps or loads needed program code and data.

stages.title: Execute
stages.text: The CPU follows instructions, reading and changing data in memory.

stages.title: Services
stages.text: The app requests operating-system services such as file access.

stages.title: Display
stages.text: Graphics work produces an updated screen and an event loop responds to input.

limits: Conceptual architecture; caching, virtual memory and exact implementation details vary.
misconception: Opening an app does not move all its files permanently out of storage.

terms.RAM: Working memory used by active programs.
terms.Process: A running program with managed resources.

title: How the Internet Delivers a Message
objective: Separate packet routing from reliable transport.

stages.title: Network
stages.text: A message can be divided into addressed packets.

stages.title: Route
stages.text: Routers forward each packet toward its destination using routing information.

stages.title: Delay
stages.text: Packets can take different paths, arrive late or be lost.

stages.title: Transport
stages.text: A reliable transport such as TCP detects missing data and retransmits it.

stages.title: Reassemble
stages.text: The receiver reconstructs the ordered application data.

limits: Three-packet teaching network; fixed illustrative delays. Does not implement TCP or internet routing.
misconception: Routers forward packets; they do not guarantee application-level order or delivery.

terms.Packet: An addressed unit of transmitted data.

title: How Wi-Fi Connects Devices
objective: Distinguish local radio airtime from internet connectivity.

stages.title: Local link
stages.text: A device communicates by radio with an access point.

stages.title: Association
stages.text: The device joins the local wireless network using its configured security.

stages.title: Airtime
stages.text: Devices sharing a channel take turns; interference and contention can reduce useful throughput.

stages.title: Gateway
stages.text: The access point’s upstream connection reaches other networks; Wi-Fi alone does not guarantee internet service.

limits: Qualitative signal and airtime indicators; no radio coverage or Mbps prediction.
misconception: Full Wi-Fi signal can coexist with a failed internet connection.

terms.Access point: Radio bridge connecting wireless devices to a network.
terms.Airtime: Time occupied on a shared radio channel.

title: How a Web Browser Loads a Page
objective: Trace a representative secure page load through rendering.

stages.title: Navigate
stages.text: The browser receives a URL and decides what resources it needs.

stages.title: DNS
stages.text: A resolver looks up the hostname’s address when needed.

stages.title: HTTPS
stages.text: A connection and TLS establish an encrypted, authenticated channel.

stages.title: Fetch
stages.text: The browser requests HTML and related styles, scripts and images.

stages.title: Render
stages.text: It builds document and style structures, lays out elements and paints pixels.

limits: Representative uncached load. HTTP versions, reuse, caching and resource ordering vary.
misconception: HTTPS protects transport; it does not prove that every page claim is true.

title: How GPS Finds Your Location
objective: Explain travel-time ranging and the receiver clock unknown.

stages.title: Signals
stages.text: Satellites broadcast timing and orbital information to receivers.

stages.title: Range
stages.text: Signal travel time gives a distance-like measurement called a pseudorange.

stages.title: Position
stages.text: Intersecting range constraints narrow possible receiver positions.

stages.title: Clock
stages.text: A typical 3D solution needs at least four satellites to solve three position coordinates and receiver clock offset.

limits: 2D illustrative range rings; no real positioning calculation. Geometry, atmosphere and clock errors affect accuracy.
misconception: GPS does not locate a receiver by having it send its position back to satellites.

terms.Pseudorange: Measured range including receiver clock error.
terms.Clock offset: Difference between receiver time and system time.

title: How a Touchscreen Detects Your Finger
objective: Connect a sensing grid’s changed capacitance to an estimated position.

stages.title: Grid
stages.text: Transparent electrodes form a sensing pattern above the display.

stages.title: Touch
stages.text: A conductive finger changes nearby electric-field coupling.

stages.title: Measure
stages.text: The controller measures changes across the electrode grid.

stages.title: Estimate
stages.text: Software estimates touch position and sends an event to the operating system.

limits: Conceptual projected-capacitive grid, not actual sensor readings. Multi-touch and noise rejection omitted.
misconception: The display does not need to be pressed like a mechanical switch.

terms.Capacitance: Ability of conductors to store separated charge.

title: How a Digital Photo Becomes an Image
objective: Distinguish optical capture, sampling and image processing.

stages.title: Camera
stages.text: A lens focuses light onto a sensor.

stages.title: Sample
stages.text: Photosites measure light at discrete locations.

stages.title: Color
stages.text: A common color-filter pattern needs processing to estimate a full-color image.

stages.title: Process
stages.text: White balance and tone processing change how sensor data is represented.

stages.title: Encode
stages.text: An image format stores the result, sometimes discarding information for smaller files.

limits: Invented 8 × 6 sample image. Not a camera sensor or compression benchmark.
misconception: A sensor records measurements; the final photo is a processed representation.

terms.Demosaicing: Estimating color from filtered sensor samples.

title: How QR Codes Store Information
objective: Identify positioning patterns and the role and limits of redundancy.

stages.title: Code
stages.text: A QR symbol combines location markers, data and error-correction information.

stages.title: Find
stages.text: Finder patterns help a decoder locate and orient the symbol.

stages.title: Read
stages.text: Modules represent encoded information under a defined format.

stages.title: Recover
stages.text: Redundancy can repair some damage, depending on level, placement and damage pattern.

limits: Non-decodable schematic, not a real QR code. Outcomes are predefined examples, not a decoder or universal damage threshold.
misconception: A fixed percentage of visible damage does not always predict successful decoding.

terms.Error correction: Redundant information used to recover damaged data.

title: How Files Get Compressed
objective: Compare exact reconstruction with deliberate information loss.

stages.title: Original
stages.text: A file is a sequence of symbols or measurements.

stages.title: Lossless
stages.text: Repeated symbols can be represented compactly without changing the decoded sequence.

stages.title: Decode
stages.text: A matching decoder reconstructs every original symbol.

stages.title: Lossy
stages.text: Quantizing measurements discards detail; the exact original cannot generally be recovered.

limits: Toy run-length representation and three numeric samples. Size comparison excludes format headers and metadata.
misconception: Compression does not always shrink every possible file.

sources.title: University of Canterbury CS Field Guide: run-length encoding

terms.Quantization: Rounding measurements to fewer possible values.

title: How an AI Language Model Generates Text
objective: Distinguish learned prediction, inference and factual reliability.

stages.title: Model
stages.text: Training adjusts model parameters using examples; inference uses those parameters.

stages.title: Context
stages.text: Input is represented as tokens that provide context for the next prediction.

stages.title: Scores
stages.text: The model produces scores over possible next tokens.

stages.title: Select
stages.text: A decoding rule chooses a token, adds it to context and repeats.

stages.title: Check
stages.text: Plausible wording can still be false; generated text needs verification.

control.label: Illustrative next token
options: The cat sat on the → mat
The cat sat on the → chair
The cat sat on the → moon

limits: Manually assigned toy options, not a real model, measured probability distribution or display of hidden reasoning.
misconception: A fluent continuation is not proof of knowledge, truth or conscious understanding.

sources.title: Google: introduction to large language models

terms.Token: A unit of text representation, often a word part.
terms.Inference: Using a trained model to produce outputs.

title: How Your Heart Circulates Blood
objective: Trace the pulmonary and systemic circuits through four chambers.

stages.title: Double circuit
stages.text: The right heart serves the lungs; the left heart serves the body.

stages.title: Right heart
stages.text: Blood from the body enters the right atrium, then right ventricle through a valve.

stages.title: Lungs
stages.text: The pulmonary artery carries blood toward lungs, where gas exchange occurs.

stages.title: Left heart
stages.text: Pulmonary veins return blood to the left atrium and ventricle.

stages.title: Body
stages.text: The left ventricle pumps through the aorta; valves help prevent backward flow.

limits: Schematic circulation, not anatomy to scale or a timing model. Oxygenation shown by labels as well as color.
misconception: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; the pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood.

sources.title: NHLBI: blood flow through the heart

title: How Your Lungs Exchange Gases
objective: Connect breathing mechanics to diffusion at alveoli.

stages.title: Respiration
stages.text: Airways bring air to alveoli alongside blood capillaries.

stages.title: Inhale
stages.text: Diaphragm contraction enlarges the chest; pressure changes draw air inward.

stages.title: Exchange
stages.text: Oxygen diffuses into blood and carbon dioxide diffuses into alveolar air down partial-pressure gradients.

stages.title: Exhale
stages.text: During quiet breathing, relaxation and elastic recoil move air outward.

limits: Simplified healthy quiet breathing; relative gas arrows, no clinical measurements.
misconception: Lungs do not pump oxygen directly into cells; blood transports it.

terms.Alveolus: Tiny air sac with a thin exchange surface.
terms.Diffusion: Net movement down a concentration or partial-pressure gradient.

title: How Your Ear Hears Sound
objective: Trace vibration to neural signaling and distinguish pitch from amplitude.

stages.title: Hearing path
stages.text: Sound travels through outer, middle and inner ear.

stages.title: Eardrum
stages.text: Pressure changes vibrate the eardrum.

stages.title: Middle ear
stages.text: Small bones transmit vibration to the inner-ear fluid.

stages.title: Cochlea
stages.text: Motion bends sensory hair bundles, initiating signals carried by the auditory nerve.

limits: Silent schematic, no sound exposure or hearing test. Loudness depends on more than amplitude alone.
misconception: The auditory nerve carries electrical signals, not a tiny sound wave.

terms.Cochlea: Spiral inner-ear structure containing sensory cells.
terms.Frequency: Cycles per second, associated with pitch.

title: How Your Eyes Form an Image
objective: Connect refraction, pupil opening and retinal sensing.

stages.title: Eye
stages.text: Cornea and lens focus incoming light toward the retina.

stages.title: Light control
stages.text: The iris changes pupil opening, regulating entering light.

stages.title: Focus
stages.text: The lens changes shape to help focus at different distances.

stages.title: Signal
stages.text: Retinal cells convert light into neural signals; the brain interprets them.

limits: Schematic rays, no optical prescription or eye examination. Not to scale.
misconception: The lens is not the only focusing surface; the cornea provides much of the refraction.

terms.Retina: Light-sensitive tissue lining the back of the eye.
terms.Accommodation: Changing lens shape to adjust focus.

title: How Digestion Breaks Down Food
objective: Separate breakdown, absorption and elimination.

stages.title: Digestive tract
stages.text: Food travels through mouth, esophagus, stomach and intestines.

stages.title: Break down
stages.text: Chewing and muscular mixing physically break food apart.

stages.title: Digest
stages.text: Enzymes and other secretions chemically break nutrients into absorbable forms.

stages.title: Absorb
stages.text: The small intestine absorbs most nutrients; the large intestine absorbs water and forms stool.

stages.title: Eliminate
stages.text: Remaining material exits; this differs from absorbing useful nutrients.

limits: Representative mixed meal; no individual transit times or dietary advice.
misconception: Most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine, not the stomach.

terms.Enzyme: Molecule that accelerates a chemical reaction.
terms.Absorption: Movement of digested nutrients into circulation.

title: How Muscles Move a Joint
objective: Explain opposing muscle groups and tendon force.

stages.title: Elbow
stages.text: Bones meet at a joint; tendons connect muscles to bones.

stages.title: Flex
stages.text: Flexor contraction pulls on the forearm to bend the elbow.

stages.title: Extend
stages.text: Extensor contraction pulls to straighten the elbow.

stages.title: Coordinate
stages.text: The nervous system coordinates activation; opposing muscles may stabilize a joint together.

limits: Two-muscle schematic; no anatomy-specific force, load or clinical range.
misconception: Muscles pull through tension; they do not actively push a bone away.

terms.Tendon: Connective tissue transmitting muscle pull to bone.
terms.Antagonist: Muscle acting in opposition to another movement.

title: How Your Kidneys Filter Blood
objective: Distinguish filtration, reabsorption and secretion.

stages.title: Nephron
stages.text: A filter and tubule process part of the blood’s fluid.

stages.title: Filter
stages.text: Water and small substances pass into the nephron; cells and most large proteins remain in blood.

stages.title: Reabsorb
stages.text: Useful substances and much water return from tubule to blood.

stages.title: Secrete
stages.text: Other substances move from blood into the tubule.

stages.title: Urine
stages.text: Fluid remaining after processing flows toward collection and elimination.

limits: Healthy simplified nephron, no quantities, diagnosis or individual kidney function.
misconception: Kidneys do more than strain out dirt; they selectively return and secrete substances.

sources.title: NIDDK: kidneys and how they work

title: How Your Body Controls Temperature
objective: Describe negative feedback and several heat-transfer responses.

stages.title: Feedback
stages.text: Temperature signals are integrated with other information by the nervous system.

stages.title: Warm
stages.text: Skin blood-flow changes can help transfer heat; evaporation of sweat removes heat.

stages.title: Cold
stages.text: Reduced skin blood flow limits heat loss; shivering increases heat production.

stages.title: Regulate
stages.text: Responses change as conditions change. Body temperature varies with person, time and measurement site.

limits: Qualitative healthy-response model. No universal target temperature or medical assessment.
misconception: Sweat cools most effectively when it evaporates, not merely when it appears.

terms.Negative feedback: A response that counteracts a change.

title: How a Reflex Works
objective: Trace a withdrawal reflex without confusing it with later awareness.

stages.title: Reflex system
stages.text: A sensory input can activate a spinal response pathway.

stages.title: Sense
stages.text: A receptor initiates a signal along a sensory neuron.

stages.title: Integrate
stages.text: Spinal circuitry connects the input to motor pathways.

stages.title: Respond
stages.text: Motor neurons activate muscle; signals also ascend toward the brain for awareness.

limits: Simplified withdrawal reflex involving interneurons. Not all reflexes share this exact circuit.
misconception: A rapid spinal response does not mean the brain never receives information.

terms.Interneuron: Neuron linking other neurons within a circuit.

title: How Vaccines Prepare the Immune System
objective: Connect antigen recognition, adaptive response and immune memory.

stages.title: Preparation
stages.text: Vaccines present antigens or instructions for producing them in different ways.

stages.title: Recognize
stages.text: Immune cells recognize relevant antigen features.

stages.title: Respond
stages.text: Adaptive responses expand selected cells; antibodies and cellular responses can contribute.

stages.title: Remember
stages.text: Some cells persist and can support a faster response to later exposure.

stages.title: Limits
stages.text: Development takes time; protection varies by vaccine, pathogen and person and can wane.

limits: Conceptual immune-cell story, no numerical effectiveness or personal vaccination recommendation.
misconception: Protection is neither instant nor an impenetrable shield.

terms.Antigen: Feature that can be recognized by an adaptive immune response.

title: Where Tap Water Comes From
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Follow a representative surface-water treatment and delivery path.

stages.title: Source
stages.text: A utility draws water from a river, lake or groundwater source.

stages.title: Clarify
stages.text: In this surface-water example, coagulation and settling remove suspended particles.

stages.title: Filter
stages.text: Water passes through filtration to remove additional material.

stages.title: Disinfect
stages.text: Controlled disinfection reduces harmful microorganisms.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.text: Storage and distribution carry treated water to household plumbing.

limits: Representative municipal surface-water process. Treatment varies with source, contaminants and local requirements.
misconception: Clear-looking water is not necessarily safe to drink.

terms.Coagulation: Helping small particles join into larger clumps.

title: What Happens After You Flush
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Trace municipal wastewater and distinguish liquid and solids pathways.

stages.title: Collection
stages.text: Sewers carry wastewater toward treatment; septic systems follow a different local process.

stages.title: Screen
stages.text: Screens and settling remove debris and some solids.

stages.title: Biology
stages.text: Microorganisms consume organic matter under managed conditions.

stages.title: Separate
stages.text: Solids settle out and need further treatment; liquid continues.

stages.title: Finish
stages.text: Disinfection and other required steps precede permitted discharge or reuse.

limits: Representative municipal system. Local treatment stages and reuse requirements vary; no septic-system simulation.
misconception: A wastewater plant does not make every incoming substance disappear.

terms.Aeration: Adding air to support biological treatment.

title: How a Grocery Store Gets Stocked
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Connect demand forecasts to orders and physical replenishment.

stages.title: Demand
stages.text: Sales history and expected events inform a forecast.

stages.title: Order
stages.text: Stores and distribution centers order against expected demand and inventory.

stages.title: Supply
stages.text: Manufacturing and suppliers replenish warehouses.

stages.title: Receive
stages.text: Transport delivers stock; receiving checks quantities and condition.

stages.title: Shelf
stages.text: Staff replenish shelves and new sales feed the next forecast.

limits: Fictional one-product store with 15 on hand and 5 safety-stock units. No lead-time or spoilage optimization.
misconception: A forecast is an estimate, not a guarantee of tomorrow’s sales.

title: How a Paycheck Works
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Calculate fictional net pay and separate withholding from final tax.

stages.title: Gross
stages.text: Gross pay is compensation before deductions.

stages.title: Benefits
stages.text: Some deductions pay for benefits; their tax treatment varies.

stages.title: Withholding
stages.text: Employers withhold taxes under applicable rules and worker information.

stages.title: Net
stages.text: Net pay is what remains after deductions.

stages.title: Reconcile
stages.text: Withholding is a payment toward tax; final liability is determined separately.

limits: Fictional US example: $1000 gross, $150 tax withholding, optional $50 retirement and $30 benefit. No tax-rate calculation or advice.
misconception: Withholding is not necessarily the final amount of tax owed.

title: How a Card Payment Reaches a Business
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Distinguish approval from movement of settled funds.

stages.title: Payment system
stages.text: Customer, merchant, processor, network and issuing and acquiring banks exchange information.

stages.title: Authorize
stages.text: The issuer approves or declines a request; approval can reserve available funds.

stages.title: Capture
stages.text: The merchant submits the approved amount for financial processing.

stages.title: Clear
stages.text: Participants exchange transaction records and determine obligations.

stages.title: Settle
stages.text: Funds move between participating institutions and the merchant is funded under its agreement.

limits: Fictional $100 sale and $3 illustrative fee; timing, fees and exact actors vary. No live payment or promised settlement time.
misconception: Authorization is not the same as money already being deposited to the merchant.

title: How a Package Reaches Your Door
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Explain physical routing and the limits of tracking scans.

stages.title: Label
stages.text: A label links the parcel to routing and service information.

stages.title: Collect
stages.text: The carrier accepts the package and records an event.

stages.title: Sort
stages.text: Facilities group packages by destination and service.

stages.title: Transport
stages.text: Line-haul transport connects hubs; local stations prepare delivery routes.

stages.title: Deliver
stages.text: A final-mile route brings the parcel to its destination; scans update tracking.

limits: Fictional route and status events, no carrier service promise or real tracking.
misconception: Label creation alone does not prove the carrier has received the package.

terms.Scan: Recorded event, not continuous GPS position.

title: How Traffic Signals Coordinate an Intersection
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Distinguish green phases, clearance and pedestrian timing.

stages.title: Controller
stages.text: A controller schedules compatible movements and receives detector requests.

stages.title: Green
stages.text: One vehicle direction is permitted while conflicting traffic remains stopped.

stages.title: Clear
stages.text: Yellow and then all-red intervals provide a transition before conflicting green.

stages.title: Pedestrian
stages.text: Walk and clearance intervals serve crossing demand; a request waits for a compatible phase.

limits: Invented isolated junction. No real traffic-control timing, adaptive algorithm or road-design guidance.
misconception: A pedestrian button generally requests service; it does not instantly stop all traffic.

terms.Clearance: Transition time before conflicting movement begins.

title: How a Plant Turns Sunlight into Growth
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Connect carbon fixation, sugars, nutrients and respiration.

stages.title: Plant system
stages.text: Leaves, roots and transport tissues connect light, air and water.

stages.title: Photosynthesis
stages.text: Light energy supports making sugars from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.

stages.title: Build
stages.text: Sugars provide carbon and energy resources for new tissues.

stages.title: Roots
stages.text: Roots supply water and mineral nutrients needed for function and growth.

stages.title: Respire
stages.text: Plants also respire, using organic molecules to release usable energy, day and night.

limits: Qualitative resource-limitation model, not a growth-rate prediction. Nutrients also matter.
misconception: Most carbon in plant dry mass comes from atmospheric CO₂, not from soil.

terms.Respiration: Processes releasing usable energy from organic molecules.

title: How Clouds Form and Rain Falls
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Separate invisible water vapor, condensation and precipitation growth.

stages.title: Moist air
stages.text: Air contains invisible water vapor.

stages.title: Cool
stages.text: Rising air expands and cools; it can reach saturation.

stages.title: Condense
stages.text: Water condenses on tiny particles, forming droplets, or ice develops in suitable conditions.

stages.title: Grow
stages.text: Droplets collide and combine or ice processes build larger particles.

stages.title: Fall
stages.text: Particles fall as precipitation when growth and air motions allow; they may evaporate before reaching ground.

limits: Conceptual parcel, no weather forecast, fixed cloud base or computed humidity.
misconception: Clouds are visible droplets or ice, not the invisible vapor itself.

terms.Saturation: Condition at which air is in equilibrium with liquid water or ice at that temperature.

title: How a Bridge Carries Weight
category: Everyday systems and the natural world
objective: Trace loads through different structural forms to foundations.

stages.title: Load path
stages.text: Deck loads must reach supports and foundations.

stages.title: Beam
stages.text: Bending causes compression on one side and tension on the other.

stages.title: Arch
stages.text: An arch carries much of its load in compression and pushes outward at supports.

stages.title: Suspension
stages.text: Tension in main cables carries deck loads to towers and anchorages.

stages.title: Foundation
stages.text: Supports transfer forces to the ground; design must consider many loads and failure modes.

limits: Qualitative static load paths, no stress, capacity or structural safety calculation.
misconception: A bridge’s apparent shape alone does not determine its safe load capacity.
